<a id="grammar"></a>

# Grammar

The grammar gate is part of the core, not an editor hook. Every prose write is checked before the snapshot, so a refused change never reaches the store.

`grammar.policy` is `block` or `warn`. `block` refuses a change with findings; `warn` stores the change and reports the findings. There is deliberately no off switch.

The check talks to a LanguageTool server over HTTP. Fenced code blocks and inline code are masked before the request, so command examples and identifiers do not produce prose findings. Markdown structure is masked the same way and for the same reason: emphasis markers, list and blockquote markers, table pipes, link destinations, reference definitions and inline HTML tags never reach the server, while the prose they wrap stays. The mask is language independent and keeps every byte offset, so a finding still reports the body position it came from. A rule artifact that survives the mask is dropped by a small table keyed by the emitted rule, reported in the payload as `masked` with its rule, count and reason, and printed by the text form, so no finding disappears silently.

`grammar.timeout` is the watchdog interval and defaults to five seconds; the cap is three intervals. The request has no hard deadline. While it runs, the gate probes the server once per interval and keeps waiting for the same request, so a slow but healthy server is not abandoned, and no check is sent twice. A server that stays silent for the whole cap is reported as `grammar.timeout`; only a server that stops answering the probe triggers the start attempt.

The check language is book data. A book may declare one with `book set <id> language <id>`; without it `grammar.language` applies, then `en-US`. Every request and every paragraph chunk carries that one language. `grammar languages` prints the supported set, the configured default and an optional book language from a ten-minute cache in the temp grammar state. `auto` is a diagnostic for `grammar check --file` and `--raw` only: a write path refuses it, and a language the server does not report is reported as `grammar.language-unsupported`, never replaced by a fallback.

The gate covers every prose path: body set, append and prepend, body replace, index prose, the footer, note blocks and layout notes. A dry run performs the same check.

`grammar check` checks a block, a file or raw text. Findings carry a line, a column, a rule, a message and the available replacements; the output is JSON or a short text summary. An incomplete check reports `checked: false` with a stable `reason` and one warning, so it never looks like a clean result. `--require-check` turns that skip into a failure for CI and release gates.

`--language` names the language for `--file` and `--raw`; `auto` reports the detected language code. A `--book` check uses the declared book language and refuses `--language`.

`grammar apply` re-checks the body, applies server-provided replacements from right to left, guards the count with `--expect`, writes once and reports the remaining findings. Only findings with one replacement are applied by `--all-safe`.

The server lifecycle is shared and explicit. `grammar serve` starts or attaches to one server, `server-info` probes it and `server-stop` stops the recorded process. State, lock and log live in the temporary directory, never in the store.

Terms suppress findings case-insensitively in two layers: `terms.txt` is global, and one file per language lives at `terms/<language>.txt`; the effective set is the union for the book's language. A term silences every finding whose span touches it, whatever rule produced it, so an inflected proper name such as `Unabhängigen Bundes` is covered by the registered `Unabhängiger Bund`. A term matches whole words by default; a leading `~` makes it a substring (`~ark` hides Arkansas too). Every suppression names its term, layer, match form and field, so nothing disappears silently, and a term never rewrites text: `grammar apply` cannot select a suppressed finding. A request never writes a file: `terms set` and `terms delete` need `--scope global|<code>` or `--book <id>`, carry a reason, and `terms commit --confirm` is the only writer. `terms check --term <t> --scope global|<code> [--all]` asks the server whether a term is an ordinary word; a real word is reported because it would hide findings.

A practical loop is check, fix the blocking findings, apply the safe single-replacement findings, re-check and then sync. A server that cannot answer is visible as an unchecked result with a `grammar.*` reason and one warning, never as a success with zero findings; `block` still refuses only on findings, so a missing server never blocks prose writes. An unchecked check before or after `grammar apply` leaves the body unchanged.
